_note: DRAFT for wiring. Offsets are metres from the image centre = site point = patch centre (north +, east +): lat_offset_m north, lon_offset_m east. Pixel is in the 2048x2048 tier2-lroc.jpg (x right, y down; centre 1024,1024). Positions of non-LM objects = observed LM pixel + LROC relative offset, because the frames carry a few metres of registration error vs the 2016 LROC coordinates.

hotspot_annotations.label: Eagle descent stage
source: https://lroc.im-ldi.com/geojson/luna_apollo_11_hardware.geojson (Landing Module, same coordinates); LROC Site Images page apollo-11/site_images/m175124932r feature pixel line 33482 sample 1887 = same point
hotspot_annotations.confidence: one source (three LROC products agree; the object is unmistakable in the frame)
hotspot_annotations.explain_en: The lower half of the Apollo 11 Lunar Module Eagle. It stayed on the Moon when the ascent stage lifted the crew off after the July 1969 landing.

hotspot_annotations.label: Passive seismometer (PSEP)
source: https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=1969-059C (EASEP: passive seismometer, 0.6735 N 23.4730 E, "about 17 m south of the LM"; 4-decimal coordinates, ~10 m from LROC)
hotspot_annotations.confidence: two sources (LROC + NASA NSSDCA; agree on area to ~10 m, pixel from LROC)
hotspot_annotations.explain_en: The Passive Seismic Experiment of the Early Apollo Scientific Experiments Package, set up south of the Lunar Module on 21 July 1969 to record moonquakes and impacts.

hotspot_annotations.label: Laser retroreflector (LRRR)
source: https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=1969-059C ("deployed about 5 meters NNW of the EASEP"; LROC layer puts it 6.7 m N of the seismometer)
hotspot_annotations.confidence: two sources (LROC layer + NASA NSSDCA relative position)
hotspot_annotations.explain_en: The Laser Ranging Retroreflector Array left by Apollo 11: a reflector that lets observatories on Earth time laser pulses bounced back from the Moon. Placed about 5 m north-north-west of the seismometer package.

dropped.reason: LROC layer position only (12 m WNW of LM); nothing resolvable at 0.4 m/px and 41 deg incidence. TV camera (LROC layer, 19 m NW of LM): nothing resolvable.

hotspot_annotations.label: Intrepid descent stage
hotspot_annotations.confidence: one source (LROC products agree; object unmistakable in the frame)
hotspot_annotations.explain_en: The lower half of the Apollo 12 Lunar Module Intrepid, left on the Moon after the November 1969 landing close to the earlier Surveyor 3 probe.

hotspot_annotations.label: ALSEP central station
source: https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=1969-099C (central station 3.0094 S, 23.4246 W; ~16 m from LROC)
hotspot_annotations.confidence: two sources (LROC + NASA NSSDCA; agree on area to ~16 m, pixel from LROC, hardware cluster visible under the ring)
hotspot_annotations.explain_en: The Apollo 12 Lunar Surface Experiments Package, deployed on 19 November 1969. Its instruments included a passive seismometer, a magnetometer and a solar wind spectrometer, all wired to the central station.

hotspot_annotations.label: Surveyor 3 lander
source: https://lroc.im-ldi.com/posts/141 (LROC post "First Look: Apollo 12 and Surveyor 3": annotated image labels descent stage, ALSEP and Surveyor 3; a different frame, M104662862R)
https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=1967-035A (landing 20 April 1967, coordinates quoted from LRO images; "within about 180 m" of the Apollo 12 LM)
hotspot_annotations.confidence: two sources (LROC table + LROC labelled image; NSSDCA repeats the LROC coordinates, not independent)
hotspot_annotations.explain_en: NASA robotic lander that touched down on 20 April 1967 on the inner slope of a small crater. Apollo 12 landed within about 180 m of it in November 1969.

dropped.reason: LROC layer position (15 m NNW of LM); only a 1-px dark speck under the ring, not identifiable.
Same site as the ALSEP point (2.7 m away), would overlap; merged into ALSEP. Same for A14, A15, A16 PSE points (1.5-3 m from ALSEP).

held.label: ALSEP central station
held.reason: HELD: the computed ring (LM-relative) lands ~4-5 m from the only visible candidate, a bright dot with a dark smudge and a track starting at it (about 9 px W of the ring). Sources agree with each other but the image offset is bigger than their stated uncertainty (0.4 m), so identification would rest on the shape. Not annotated.

dropped.reason: LROC layer position 1.33 km E of the LM: outside the 922 m frame.

hotspot_annotations.label: Falcon descent stage
hotspot_annotations.confidence: two sources (LROC + NASA NSSDCA identical coordinates)
hotspot_annotations.explain_en: The lower half of the Apollo 15 Lunar Module Falcon, left on the Moon after the July 1971 landing.

hotspot_annotations.label: ALSEP central station
source: https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=1971-063C (ALSEP 26.1341 N, 3.6298 E; equals LROC PSE point; "deployed at the end of the traverse" on the first EVA)
hotspot_annotations.confidence: two sources (LROC + NASA NSSDCA, within ~3 m)
hotspot_annotations.explain_en: The Apollo 15 Lunar Surface Experiments Package, deployed on 31 July 1971. Instruments listed by NASA: passive seismometer, magnetometer, solar wind spectrometer, suprathermal ion detector, cold cathode ion gauge, dust detector and a heat flow experiment.

hotspot_annotations.label: Lunar Roving Vehicle
hotspot_annotations.confidence: one source (LROC table and layer; dark rover blob at the end of a track under the ring)
hotspot_annotations.explain_en: Apollo 15 was the first mission to carry a Lunar Roving Vehicle. This is where LROC finds it after the last drive; it was left on the Moon.

hotspot_annotations.label: Orion descent stage
hotspot_annotations.confidence: one source (LROC products agree; object unmistakable in the frame)
hotspot_annotations.explain_en: The lower half of the Apollo 16 Lunar Module Orion, left on the Moon after the April 1972 landing.

hotspot_annotations.label: ALSEP central station
source: https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/nmc/spacecraft/display.action?id=1972-031C (central station 8.9754 S, 15.4981 E; ~20 m from LROC, "turned on at 19:38 UT on 21 April 1972")
hotspot_annotations.confidence: two sources (LROC + NASA NSSDCA; agree on area to ~20 m, pixel from LROC, hardware cluster visible under the ring)
hotspot_annotations.explain_en: The Apollo 16 Lunar Surface Experiments Package, switched on 21 April 1972. NASA lists a passive seismometer, an active seismometer, a magnetometer and a heat flow experiment.

hotspot_annotations.label: Lunar Roving Vehicle

hotspot_annotations.explain_en: The Apollo 16 Lunar Roving Vehicle as LROC finds it after the mission; it was left on the Moon.

hotspot_annotations.explain_en: The lower half of the Apollo 17 Lunar Module Challenger, left on the Moon after the December 1972 landing, the last crewed landing so far.

hotspot_annotations.confidence: one source (LROC table and layer; dark rover blob at the end of a track under the ring)

held.label: ALSEP central station
held.reason: HELD: ring falls on a speckled dark patch; scattered bright dots around it, none unambiguous (the A17 frame is a heavy contrast stretch). Not annotated.

held.label: SEP transmitter
held.reason: HELD: ring sits on a crossing of rover tracks; the SEP is a small object and nothing identifiable is resolved. Position-only, one source, not verifiable by eye. Not annotated.

dropped_global.reason: LROC publishes EVA path polylines (luna_apollo_NN_eva*, luna_apollo_11_traverse) and EVA station points (unlabelled at Apollo 12, mostly outside the frame, not hardware); no source labels track clusters on these frames. Not annotated.
